Last in, first out. Also where your local variables live.

Membership without duplicates.

Double-ended queue, pronounced "deck."
Behind C++ std::map, Java’s TreeMap and the Linux scheduler’s run queue.
Adelson-Velsky and Landis, 1962. The first self-balancing binary search tree.
Bayer and McCreight, 1970, at Boeing. Nobody is sure what the B stands for.
Fixed size, wraps around. Perfect for streams and logs.

Range queries and updates in O(log n).

Near-constant time per operation: the inverse Ackermann function.
Ralph Merkle, 1979. Behind git, Bitcoin and certificate transparency.
How sparse graphs are usually stored.

Tree plus heap: random priorities keep it balanced.

Emacs’s text buffer: a gap that moves with the cursor.

Split 2D space into four, recursively.

O’Neil and colleagues, 1996. Behind LevelDB, RocksDB and Cassandra.

Conflict-free replicated data type. Merge in any order, get the same result.

Hinze and Paterson, 2006. Haskell’s Data.Sequence.
Gérard Huet, 1997. A movable cursor into an immutable structure.
O(log log U) operations on integer keys.
Simple, fast in practice, and its exact bounds are still being worked out.

Rank and select queries over sequences, in compressed space.
